findings.checklist_item: - [ ] AC6/§5: reference the existing scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py (bug dcc3) prior art and justify why a new runtime observability probe is needed rather than reusing/extending it — specifically naming the runtime-metric vs apply-time-one-shot distinction, or reuse its pure-function join core.
evidence: Plan AC6: 'observability compares the rendered Terraform-declared volumes/mounts manifest with /proc/mounts and lsblk, emits a metric, and fails visibly when declaration/state and live mounts diverge.'

scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:6-20 already performs this join: 'Terraform holds one half of the answer (which volumes are attached to which instance) and the host holds the other (which mount points are backed by a real filesystem)... This script performs that join and fails loudly.'

scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:181 HOST_PROBE = 'lsblk -P -o NAME,SERIAL,MOUNTPOINT' and attachments_from_plan() reading `terraform show -json` (lines 80-96) — the declared-vs-provisioned comparison AC6 describes.

The dcc3 script is created for the identical failure mode AC6 targets: 'a volume attached by terraform apply AFTER first boot is never mounted... a closed story sat provably not-in-effect for days' (scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:2-14).

It is already documented in the runbook this plan depends on: infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md:286 'scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py performs that join. Run it after this procedure', and its design is referenced in infra/scripts/observability.sh:582.
The plan text never mentions assert_volumes_in_service.py or the dcc3 bug, so the anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three novelty question is unaddressed.
findings.finding: AC6 proposes a new runtime declared-vs-provisioned check (Terraform-declared volumes/mounts joined against live /proc/mounts + lsblk, emitting a metric) without acknowledging the existing repo prior art scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py (bug dcc3), which already performs the same declared-vs-provisioned join (Terraform aws_volume_attachment vs live `lsblk -P -o NAME,SERIAL,MOUNTPOINT`, failing loudly with in-service/NOT-IN-SERVICE/UNKNOWN outcomes). The plan does not justify building a new probe versus reusing or extending the existing one.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC6 / §5 'Land the declared-vs-provisioned check through Gerrit'
scenarios: Author implements a new probe from scratch that duplicates the dcc3 join logic, creating a second source of truth for declared-vs-provisioned reconciliation.

The genuine gap (dcc3 is an apply-time one-shot; AC6 wants a recurring runtime metric) is real but goes unstated, so a reviewer cannot tell whether the new check is justified novelty or unnecessary repackaging.
findings.suggested_fix: In §5 and AC6, cite scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py as prior art, state that its Terraform-attachment/lsblk join logic (attachments_from_plan + parse_host_mounts + classify, already unit-tested) should be reused rather than re-implemented, and scope the new work explicitly to the delta: a recurring observability tick that emits a CloudWatch metric (the dcc3 script is an apply-time/operation-linked one-shot with no metric).

findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion / test that injects a declared-vs-live mount divergence (e.g. an unmounted or mismatched entry) and asserts the check fails and the metric reflects the mismatch — not just the all-matching happy path.
evidence: 'fails visibly when declaration/state and live mounts diverge' is asserted as the value but only 'local verification' is required with no divergence-injection test
The check's stated raison d'être is the S1 mode 'where Terraform declaration/state and live mount reality diverge' — the failure path is the point
E5: a NEW flow whose happy-path-only tests omit the failure path, and the risk of a check that never proves it detects the condition it targets
findings.finding: AC6 introduces new logic (the declared-vs-provisioned check whose entire purpose is to catch the S1 divergence mode) but no acceptance criterion or test scenario proves the DIVERGENCE-DETECTION failure path — i.e. that with a deliberately induced mismatch between the rendered Terraform manifest and live /proc/mounts+lsblk, the check actually fails/flags. Coverage that only exercises the matching (happy) path can go green while never proving the check catches the very divergence it exists to detect.
findings.location: AC6 / 'Land the declared-vs-provisioned check' (Live work item 5)
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC7: 'With a simulated divergence (declared mount absent from /proc/mounts or lsblk), the check emits the failing metric and exits non-zero; with declarations matching live state it passes — both cases covered by a test that lands through Gerrit.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in AC6 whether the declared-vs-provisioned check EXTENDS check-mounts.sh / observability.sh §2e (which already own the /proc/mounts read and the gate_scratch_mounted metric) or introduces a new component, and justify any new code path that re-implements live mount reconciliation.
evidence: Plan AC6: 'observability compares the rendered Terraform-declared volumes/mounts manifest with /proc/mounts and lsblk, emits a metric'

infra/scripts/check-mounts.sh:51-52 already reads /proc/mounts to decide mountedness for /var/gerrit and /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch, but against a hardcoded list (line 37), not a rendered Terraform manifest, and emits no metric
infra/scripts/observability.sh:351-354 already publishes gate_scratch_mounted as a per-tick heartbeat metric

The genuinely-new part (rendering the Terraform-declared manifest for runtime comparison) is justified — the plan affirmatively states the static/state-only mode 'can miss the S1 mode where Terraform declaration/state and live mount reality diverge' — so this is extend-vs-rebuild scoping, not an NIH rejection
findings.finding: AC6's runtime declared-vs-provisioned check overlaps functionally with two existing components — check-mounts.sh (already reconciles live mounts via /proc/mounts against an expected list) and observability.sh §2e (already emits the gate_scratch_mounted metric per tick) — but the plan does not state whether AC6 extends them or builds a parallel implementation.
findings.location: AC6 / 'Live work this ticket still owns' item 5
scenarios: Author writes a fresh script that re-derives /proc/mounts reconciliation logic already in check-mounts.sh, creating two sources of truth for 'is this mount live' that can drift
A second metric-emission path is added alongside observability.sh §2e's gate_scratch_mounted, duplicating the per-tick publisher wiring
findings.suggested_fix: Scope AC6 to add the Terraform-declared-manifest rendering + comparison into the existing observability probe (which already emits gate_scratch_mounted) and reuse check-mounts.sh's /proc/mounts logic, following the established '--print-volumes' manifest-rendering precedent (compose-up.sh, docker-storage-cap.sh) rather than a standalone reconciler.

findings.checklist_item: State the disposition for the check's own evaluation failure (manifest unrenderable / lsblk|/proc/mounts unreadable) distinctly from a genuine declared-vs-live divergence, and what metric value/exit each surfaces.
evidence: 'the observability probe must compare ... and emit a metric ... fails visibly when ... diverge'
No disposition word (transient/retryable vs fatal) stated for the probe's own read/render failure as opposed to a true divergence
Advisory criterion — coaches per-arm disposition before the mechanism ships
findings.finding: The declared-vs-provisioned check adds a new failure-signalling path ('fails visibly ... emit a metric') but the plan does not state the disposition when the check itself cannot evaluate — e.g. the rendered manifest is unavailable, or /proc/mounts / lsblk cannot be read. Without a stated disposition, an errored probe could surface as either a false 'diverged' alarm or a silently swallowed no-op, and it is unstated whether that condition is treated distinctly from a genuine divergence.
